- When a single request uses a large context window (our embeddings + 50k token document in the same call), how do you round the billable token units? Do you charge per-request rounded up to a fixed quantum or based on per-token increments?
- If we mix Hosted with Reserved Dedicated capacity during the month (e.g., bursts hit dedicated pool but some fall back to hosted), how are discounts or reserved credits applied in proration?
- We saw a small per-call minimum on the sample invoice (looks like 150 tokens). Is that a hard floor or negotiable for pilots?

Carlos — thanks for the clear examples and for attaching the invoice. Quick answers up front, then two short worked examples so your finance team can match numbers.

Summary answers:
- Rounding quantum: Hosted API calls are rounded up to the nearest 256-token quantum for per-request accounting; Dedicated-reserved consumption is tallied at the same quantum but then offset against your committed token bundle before host charges apply.
- Mixed-mode proration: We apply reserved capacity credits first (on a daily basis). Any consumption beyond reserved capacity in a day is billed at the hosted rate and rounded per the same quantum. If a single request spans resources (KV cache + fallback), we attribute the billable tokens to the resource that served the majority of the tokens.
- Per-call minimum: The default per-request floor in your pilot tier is 150 tokens — this was included in the sample invoice. For pilots we can temporarily lower this floor to 50 tokens (for 90 days) if procurement signs the pilot amendment.

Worked examples (numbers simplified):
1) Single long-context request (50,300 tokens total, hosted response):
   - Billing quantum: 256 tokens. 50,300 / 256 = 196.3 => rounded up to 197 quanta => billable tokens = 197 * 256 = 50,432 tokens.
   - If per-request floor applies (150 tokens) it is less than rounded amount, so no change.

2) Mixed day with reserved + hosted overflow:
   - Reserved daily bundle: 1,000,000 tokens (committed). Left in day before burst: 60,000 tokens.
   - Request A (30,000 tokens) served entirely by Dedicated => consumes 30,000 of reserved. Reserved remaining: 30,000.
   - Request B (50,000 tokens) arrives, but Dedicated has only 30,000 left; 30,000 served by Dedicated, 20,000 by Hosted => we bill: 30,000 against reserved (no hosted charge) then 20,000 billed at hosted. Hosted charges apply rounding: 20,000 / 256 = 78.13 => rounded up to 79 quanta => 79*256 = 20,224 billable hosted tokens.
   - Net billing: reserved credits reduced by 60,000; hosted invoice shows 20,224 tokens for that overflow.

Notes: the invoice line you highlighted looks like the hosted rounding delta (20,224 vs 20,000). That is expected given per-request quantum rounding.

Next steps: if that aligns with your expectations, procurement can accept the pilot amendment and we’ll add the temporary 50-token floor for 90 days. I’m attaching a draft pricing schedule that lists your committed bundle and per-token hosted price for each model tier.

Adding a couple of product/ops clarifications so finance has full context: 

- Model SKU differences: quantized model variants (e.g., rw-ql8) have a ~20% lower per-token hosted price; however, dedicated bundles are priced per-GPU-hour equivalently and the internal token estimation for reserved consumption is derived from an internal throughput model, not raw token counts. For pricing reconciliation we map reserved hours -> estimated tokens and then apply the daily offset Mina described.
- Discount stacking: reserved discounts apply to the committed bundle. Additional usage discounts (volume tiers) only kick in on hosted overage once monthly thresholds are reached; we do not retroactively apply volume discounts to already billed overages in a given month.
- Edge-case: if a single request triggers fallback to multiple model SKUs mid-generation (rare), our billing attribution favors the final model that produced the response and will include a short note on the invoice line.

If procurement wants an example invoice that breaks out reserved-to-hosted attribution by timestamp, we can generate a per-request export for week 1 of the pilot (format: CSV with request_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_attributed, resource). Happy to run that and share.

-Vivek
Head of Dedicated Product, Redwood Inference
[internal note: recommend we offer 90d 50-token floor and one free overflow day for first month to reduce procurement friction]
